blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code
SpeedBlip's color palette was chosen deliberately - each color has a job.

The primary color is #22C55E (Pulse Green). It is the action color - buttons, active states, the speed gauge when your connection is healthy. Green signals good. It was the right choice for a tool whose core promise is "your internet is fine."
Here is the full palette and why each color exists:

items: #22C55E - Pulse Green (primary): healthy status, CTAs, active navigation
#16A34A - Primary Dark: hover states, pressed button states
#DCFCE7 - Primary Light: subtle backgrounds, success banners
#14B8A6 - Electric Teal (accent): charts, secondary highlights, info states
#F8FAFC - Background: the main app background - light but not harsh white
#0F172A - Text Primary: body text, headings - near-black with a blue tint
#EF4444 - Danger: speed below threshold, error states

blocks.content: Notice the logic: green for good, amber for warning, red for danger. The user never has to read a label to know the state - the color tells the story instantly.

blocks.alt: Ten color swatches laid out in a grid, each labeled with hex code and role name, color-coded from greens to teals to neutrals to warning and danger
